subject: ss-haematology
title: Inherited bleeding disorders haemophilia levels and von Willebrand disease
refs: Harrison Principles of Internal Medicine 22e Ch 121 Coagulation Disorders
Harrison Ch 120 Disorders of Platelets and Vessel Wall von Willebrand sections
WFH Guidelines for the Management of Hemophilia 2020

steps.tx: **Haemophilia** (X linked factor deficiency) affects **one** in **ten thousand** males worldwide, with **haemophilia A** (factor VIII deficiency) forming **eighty** percent of cases. **F8 gene** mutations cause haemophilia A, and **F9 gene** mutations cause haemophilia B. **Haemophilia B** forms the remaining **twenty** percent of cases. **X linked recessive** (gene on X chromosome) inheritance spares most carriers from major bleeding. **Severe disease** (factor below **1** percent) bleeds spontaneously into joints.
steps.say: Haemophilia affects one in ten thousand males worldwide. Haemophilia A forms eighty percent of all cases. Severe disease below one percent bleeds spontaneously into joints.

steps.tx: Factor level grades severity precisely. **Severe haemophilia** (below **1** percent) gives spontaneous haemarthroses (joint bleeds) without injury. **Moderate disease** (**1** to **five** percent) bleeds after minor trauma. **Mild disease** (above **five** percent) bleeds mainly during surgery or after major injury. **Haemophilia A and B** look clinically identical, so factor assay separates them. **Bleeding frequency** exceeds **thirty** joint bleeds yearly in untreated severe disease.
steps.say: Severe disease bleeds spontaneously into joints without injury. Moderate disease bleeds after minor trauma episodes. A and B haemophilia look clinically identical to clinicians.

steps.tx: **Haemarthrosis** (joint bleed) is the signature bleed of haemophilia and destroys cartilage over time. **Deep muscle bleeds** (in thigh and calf) cause compartment syndrome and pseudotumours. **Epidural and intracranial bleeds** threaten life in neonates and fall injuries. **Physiotherapy** (exercise therapy) preserves joints between bleeds. **Arthropathy** (joint destruction) was the leading disability cause before prophylaxis era.
steps.say: Haemarthrosis is the signature bleed of haemophilia disease. Deep muscle bleeds cause compartment syndrome complications. Physiotherapy preserves joints between bleeding episodes in patients today.

steps.tx: Acute bleeds need factor immediately. **Factor VIII concentrate** (replacement protein) at **fifty** units per kg raises levels to **one hundred** percent in a **seventy** kg severe patient. **1 unit per kg raises factor VIII by ~2 percent**, so **twenty five** units per kg gives roughly **fifty** percent. **Factor IX concentrate** (replacement protein) recovers less per unit, near **1** percent per unit per kg. **Prophylactic dosing** (regular prevention) cuts joint bleeds by over **ninety** percent in children.
steps.say: Factor VIII at fifty units raises levels to one hundred percent. One unit per kilogram raises factor VIII by two percent. Prophylaxis cuts joint bleeds by over ninety percent.

steps.tx: **Inhibitors** (neutralising antibodies) complicate factor replacement badly. **Bethesda units** (inhibitor assay units) quantify strength, with **five** units above clinical relevance. **Haemophilia A inhibitors** develop in **twenty five** to **thirty** percent of severe patients, and **haemophilia B** inhibitors in only **three** to **five** percent. **High risk mutations** (large deletions, nonsense mutations) predict inhibitor formation. **Immune tolerance induction** (ITI, antibody erasure therapy) removes inhibitors in about **sixty** percent.
steps.say: Inhibitors develop in twenty five to thirty percent of severe A. Bethesda units above five carry clinical relevance. Immune tolerance removes inhibitors in about sixty percent.

steps.tx: **Desmopressin** (DDAVP, hormone releasing stored factor VIII) suits mild haemophilia A with tested response. **Tranexamic acid** (antifibrinolytic drug) is dosed **twenty five** mg per kg three to four times daily for mucosal bleeds. **Non transfusion therapy** (emicizumab, gene therapy) transforms severe care. **Emicizumab** (factor VIII mimetic antibody) is given weekly or monthly by injection in haemophilia A with or without inhibitors. **Gene therapy** (AAV vector delivered factor genes) has reached licensed use in adults.
steps.say: Desmopressin suits mild haemophilia A with tested response. Tranexamic acid is dosed at twenty five milligrams per kilogram. Emicizumab allows prophylaxis by weekly injection.

steps.tx: **Von Willebrand disease** (VWD, vessel factor deficiency) is the commonest inherited bleeding disorder, affecting **1** to **2** percent of people. **Type 1** (partial deficiency) is commonest and desmopressin responsive. **Type 2** (qualitative defect) splits into **2A** (multimer loss), **2B** (platelet gain), **2M** (platelet function loss) and **2N** (factor VIII binding loss). **Type three** (near complete absence) bleeds severely with prophylaxis needs. **Ristocetin cofactor** (activity assay) confirms the diagnosis with antigen levels.
steps.say: Von Willebrand disease affects one to two percent of people. Type one is commonest and desmopressin responsive. Type three bleeds severely and needs prophylaxis.

steps.tx: **Ristocetin aggregation** (vessel factor test) patterns separate platelet receptor faults from vessel factor faults. **Bernard Soulier syndrome** (GPIb defect) shows absent ristocetin response with giant platelets. **Von Willebrand disease** also loses ristocetin response but keeps normal platelet size and count. **Factor VIII level** falls in **type 2N** disease and corrects the haemophilia A mimicry. **Multimer analysis** (clotting protein size test) grades severity and predicts treatment response.
steps.say: Ristocetin testing separates platelet receptor faults from vessel factor faults. Bernard Soulier has giant platelets with absent response. Multimer analysis grades severity and predicts response.

steps.tx: Women with bleeding disorders need explicit care. **Menorrhagia** (heavy menstrual bleeding) dominates mild haemophilia and VWD presentations in women. **FXI deficiency** (factor XI defect) raises surgical bleeding in specific populations. **Factor XIII deficiency** (clot strength defect) bleeds from the umbilical cord and warns of intracranial risk. **Postpartum haemorrhage** (delivery bleeding) deserves prophylaxis planning in known carriers.
steps.say: Menorrhagia dominates mild haemophilia and VWD presentations in women. FXI deficiency raises surgical bleeding in specific populations. Postpartum planning protects known carriers during delivery.

steps.tx: Exam stems exploit these contrasts. **Haemophilia A** is **X linked** with high joints bleeds, while **VWD type 2N** mimics A with carrier females affected. **1 unit per kg** raises factor VIII by **2** percent, a number examiners demand. **Desmopressin** works in mild haemophilia A and **type 1** VWD but fails in severe disease. **Bethesda units** quantify inhibitors, not factor levels themselves.
steps.say: Haemophilia A is X linked with joint bleeds dominant. One unit raises factor VIII by two percent. Desmopressin works in mild disease but fails in severe cases.

steps.tx: High-yield for the exam: haemophilia affects **1** in **ten thousand** males with **A forming eighty** percent. **Severe below 1** percent bleeds spontaneously, and **moderate 1 to five** percent bleeds after minor trauma. **1 unit per kg raises factor VIII** by **2** percent, and **prophylaxis** cuts bleeds above **ninety** percent. **VWD** affects **1 to 2** percent of people, and **desmopressin** treats **type 1**.
steps.say: Haemophilia A forms eighty percent of all cases. One unit per kilogram raises factor VIII by two percent. Von Willebrand disease affects one to two percent of people.
